items.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022
items.q: And today Sebastian, he’s playing his tenor and he goes [scats] I put on Volume 24, major and minor.

ctx.x: Yes. That’s when the kids that I’m working with up at Park Middle School in Jeffersonville about five miles from my house — every morning from nine to nine forty-

five — I’ve been working with them for two months. Free, just to do it. Eight saxophones. Yes there are mistakes. And today Sebastian, he’s playing his tenor and he goes [scats] I put on Volume 24, major and minor. We work with major, the B flat major scale. Today we worked with the B flat concert minor scale. We practiced the scale, practiced the arpeggio up to the ninth and back down. They couldn’t have done this two months ago at all, not at all. Anyhow, when he was playing he went up and hit the major third,…

Well thank you for saying that because I think mistakes or unintended notes — it may depend on who you’re working with and what age. But I can see how Michael Brecker — people might write out, transcribe Michael Brecker’s solos and point out that look he played a major third over a minor chord, and they will justify it. They will say it’s a color tone or watch because he does it seven measures later. It’s a bit of a conundrum I think. I was debating about whether to do this or not and I’m going to give it a try…
